chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abu Qurra, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'These people say that the earnings of the teacher are ill-gotten gain (suh't).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are lying, enemies of Allah! They merely intend that the Quran should not be taught. And if a man were to give the teacher the wergild (diyah) of his child, it would be permissible for the teacher.'
ai.seo_question: Is the salary or earnings of a Quran teacher considered halal or haram in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the claim that a teacher's earnings are 'ill-gotten gain' (suh't), attributing this view to opponents who seek to discourage Quranic education. He illustrates the permissibility of teaching earnings by citing that even a large sum like the wergild of a child is lawful for the teacher, emphasizing that knowledge transmission is a legitimate trade. This hadith underscores the high status of teachers in Shia jurisprudence, validating their compensation as a rightful reward for spiritual and intellectual guidance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Shareef Bin Sabiq, from Al Fazl Bin Abu qurra who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘They (people) are saying that the earnings of the teacher is an ill-gotten gain’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are lying, enemies of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! But rather, they are intending that they (teachers) should not be teaching the Quran, and if the teacher is given by a man wergild of his child, it would be Permissible’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Sharif ibn Sabiq from al-Fadl ibn abu Qurrah who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘They say that receiving payment for teaching is Suht (filthy and unlawful). He (the Imam) said, ‘They, the enemies of Allah, have spoken a lie. They want to stop teaching of al-Quran. If one gives blood money for his child to a teacher it (payment) is lawful for the teacher.’”
